classification.difficultyReason: Relate meeting time and remaining journey time, eliminate a variable and solve a quadratic, rejecting an infeasible speed.

content.prompt: $A$ and $B$ are two towns, $120\text{ km}$ apart. A car starts from $A$ to travel to $B$ at the same time as a second car, whose speed is $20\text{ km/h}$ faster than the first, starts from $B$ to travel to $A$. The slower car reaches $B$ $1$ hour and $48$ minutes after it passes the other car. Find their speeds.

answer.short:
Slower car: $40\text{ km/h}$. Faster car: $60\text{ km/h}$.

Use the meeting time and the slower car’s total journey time to form two equations, then eliminate the time.
answer.worked:
Let the slower car’s speed be $x\text{ km/h}$ and the time until the cars meet be $t$ hours. The faster car’s speed is $(x+20)\text{ km/h}$, and $1\text{ h }48\text{ min}=\frac95\text{ h}$.

The distances travelled before meeting total $120\text{ km}$:
$$\begin{align*}xt+(x+20)t&=120\\(2x+20)t&=120\\t&=\frac{60}{x+10}.\end{align*}$$

The slower car’s whole journey is $120\text{ km}$:
$$\begin{align*}x\left(t+\frac95\right)&=120\\x\left(\frac{60}{x+10}+\frac95\right)&=120\\300x+9x(x+10)&=600(x+10)\\9x^2-210x-6000&=0\\3x^2-70x-2000&=0\\(3x+50)(x-40)&=0\\x&=40\text{ or }-\frac{50}{3}.\end{align*}$$

Reject the negative speed. Hence the slower car travels at $40\text{ km/h}$ and the faster car at $60\text{ km/h}$.

Check: they meet after $\frac{120}{(40+60)}=1.2$ hours. The slower car’s whole journey takes $\frac{120}{40}=3$ hours, leaving $3-1.2=1.8$ hours, or $1$ hour and $48$ minutes, after meeting.
